agent_rules.source_of_truth: This file is the authoritative implementation progress tracker. Update it immediately when task or test state changes.
agent_rules.priority_rule: Jobs must be worked in ascending priority order unless a higher-priority job is blocked by an external dependency.
agent_rules.single_active_job_rule: Prefer one active implementation job at a time. Do not begin the next incomplete job until the current job satisfies its completion gate, unless the current job is explicitly blocked.
agent_rules.job_completion_rule: A job's completed field may be set to 'done' only when every task in the job is done, every required test has been written, and every required test is passing.
agent_rules.test_failure_rule: If any test associated with a job fails, that job's completed field must immediately be changed from 'done' to 'tests_failing'. The failure must be addressed before moving to the next job.
agent_rules.new_session_rule: At the beginning of every new coding-agent session, rerun the full project test suite before doing implementation work.
agent_rules.new_session_failure_rule: If the full test suite fails at session start, identify which job owns each failing test or affected component. Set each affected job's completed field to 'tests_failing'. Fix all failures before continuing to the next planned job.
agent_rules.regression_rule: Before marking any job done, run both the job-specific tests and the full regression suite.
agent_rules.no_false_completion_rule: Never mark a task or job done based only on code being written. Completion requires verified passing tests.
agent_rules.evidence_rule: When a job is marked done, record the test command and last passing timestamp in its verification section.
agent_rules.blocking_rule: If blocked, record the blocker and continue only with work that does not violate priority order or depend on the blocked component.

session_start_checklist.action: Read progress.json and identify the highest-priority job whose completed field is not 'done'.
Run the full project test suite before changing code.
If any test fails, update affected jobs to 'tests_failing' and repair them before starting new implementation work.

architecture.shape: Expo React Native application, Android target, fully on-device. No server and no PostgreSQL.
architecture.rationale: The user asked for a React Native app rather than the Next.js PWA in the specification, and chose the server-free variant. The phone fetches the school iCalendar feed directly, interprets it on-device, and stores everything in local SQLite.
supersedes: HTTP API routes under /api (spec 25) -- replaced by in-process repository functions with the same shapes
PWA manifest and service worker (spec 26) -- replaced by native install and SQLite persistence
Playwright E2E (prompt) -- replaced by React Native Testing Library screen tests
Admin review web route protected by ADMIN_SECRET (spec 27) -- replaced by a developer-only in-app screen
preserved: All domain types, taxonomies and importance rules
Deterministic class alias and time normalization
Interpreter abstraction with a swappable Gemma implementation
Deterministic relevance, change detection and notification scheduling
Local-only family configuration and the privacy posture
notes: Spec references "Gemma 4 E2B"; no Gemma 4 exists. The adapter targets any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a configurable model id, defaulting to a Gemma 3 instruct model.
The GSMNC feed publishes every event as an all-day VEVENT with times embedded in the SUMMARY text and empty DESCRIPTION/LOCATION, so time extraction is text-based rather than taken from DTSTART.
The feed contains byte sequences that are not valid UTF-8; decoding falls back per line.
The feed contains no RRULE, so recurrence expansion is not required.

summary.evaluation: 162/162 live feed events parsed and normalized; 0 classified as "other"; 0 with unresolved classes; 12 (7.4%) held for review; 66/66 stated times extracted; 0 closure-wording misclassifications
deferred: Verification against the live feed on a physical device over time
